Author: Watters, Nagy & Bellstedt, 2019
Etymology: The specific name is given in honour of Angela Watters, wife of Brian R. Watters, in recognition of her unwavering support for his many field trips to Africa to study fishes of the genus Nothobranchius, during which she also very capably maintained the fishes in the tanks of his large fish room; a noun in genitive (Ref. 122068).

Author: Nagy, Watters & Bellstedt, 2020
Etymology: The specific name is given in honour of Sir David F. Attenborough, in recognition of his dedicated efforts to promote biophilia: raising awareness of the wonders and beauties of nature for so many people worldwide, promoting awareness of the importance of biodiversity conservation, and above all, inspiring so many researchers in the field of natural history, including the authors; a noun in genitive case (Ref. 123150).

Author: Bragança & Chakona, 2022
Etymology: The specific name, balamaensis, refers to the Balama region in the Cabo Delgado Province, Mozambique, where the type locality for the species is located (Ref. 127332).

Author: Valdesalici, 2010
Etymology: The species name is dedicated to the collector, aquarist Jørn Boklund, of Denmark (Ref. 84038).

Author: Watters, Wildekamp & Shidlovskiy, 2015
Etymology: The species name capriviensis represents a toponym after the Caprivi Strip, the historical name for the narrow extension of northeastern Namibia, where this species occurs; this part of Namibia was originally named after the German statesman Count Leo von Caprivi (Ref. 116076).

Author: Watters, Cooper & Wildekamp, 2008
Etymology: The name cardinalis is in reference to the striking, dominantly red coloration of males; from the Latin cardinalis", meaning principal, chief or essential, from which the ecclesiastical title of cardinal was derived; the name as applied here is an allusion to the blood-red vesture worn by cardinals (Ref. 74420).

Author: Nagy, 2014
Etymology: The specific name is given in honour of Professor Auguste Chocha Manda of the University of Lubumbashi, Katanga, Congo DR, for his dedication to research of the ichthyofauna of the Democratic Republic of Congo (Ref. 97353).

Author: Nagy, Watters & Bellstedt, 2017
Etymology: The specific epithet is given in honour of Barry J. Cooper, renowned collector and breeder of killifish, for his significant contributions to the field study of Nothobranchius and to the killifish hobby in general; a noun in genitive (Ref. 117281).

Author: Valdesalici & Amato, 2019
Etymology: The specific name epithet is given in honour of Patrick de Rham, Lausanne, Swiss, who first discovered the new species on the 7th of July 1985 in a grassy swamp situated near Ahero on the east side of the Nakuru to Kisumu road and for his contribution on observing in the field part of the life cycle of this species; a noun in genitive (Ref. 123202).

Author: Nagy, 2014
Etymology: The species epithet flagrans is a Latin participial adjective meaning flaming, blazing, burning, glowing and is given with reference to the vivid orange-red colour of the submarginal bands of the anal and caudal fins in males (Ref. 98826).

Author: Wildekamp, Watters & Sainthouse, 2002
Etymology: From the Latin geminus meaning twin or double, in reference to the reflective silver spots in the upper part of the iris appearing as twin stars.
